title: Glycosylated Fibronectin Compared With sFlt-1/PlGF Ratio for Preeclampsia Assessment.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ratio of sFlt-1 (soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1) to PlGF (placental growth factor) is an established biomarker for preeclampsia diagnostic triage. GlyFn (glycosylated fibronectin) measured by point-of-care testing is an alternative rapid assessment from finger-stick blood samples. This study was designed to test the hypothesis that the sensitivity of GlyFn is noninferior to that of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio in women with suspected preeclampsia. METHODS: This prospective observational study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of both tests for preeclampsia in high-risk participants presenting between 24+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation at 5 hospitals from January 2024 to July 2025. Participants underwent simultaneous point-of-care GlyFn testing (Lumella) and laboratory sFlt-1/PlGF ratio measurements. The primary outcome was birth for preeclampsia within 28 days of testing. Thresholds were set at GlyFn ≥350 μg/mL and sFlt-1/PlGF ratio ≥38. The noninferiority margin was predefined at 5%. RESULTS: Among 397 participants, 59 (14.9%) had an indicated birth for preeclampsia within 28 days. GlyFn showed a sensitivity of 86.44% (95% CI, 75.02%-93.96%) compared with sFlt-1/PlGF 84.75% (95% CI, 73.01%-92.78%). Although sensitivities were numerically similar (P=0.79), the CI around the difference was too wide to establish noninferiority at the 5% margin. Negative predictive values were 96.40% and 96.59%, respectively. However, GlyFn had a lower specificity (63.31% versus 75.44%, P<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Point-of-care GlyFn testing showed similar sensitivity and negative predictive value to the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio for predicting an indicated birth for preeclampsia within 28 days. The point-of-care nature of the GlyFn test may facilitate immediate clinical decision-making in diverse healthcare settings. REGISTRATION: URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN13430018; Unique identifier: ISRCTN13430018.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO. METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed. RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI. CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

title: Practical Approaches to Coronary Venous Ethanol Ablation for Refractory Ventricular Arrhythmias: Technique Selection and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary venous ethanol ablation (CVEA) is a promising alternative for refractory ventricular arrhythmias (VAs); however, it has limited availability, lacks guideline support, and comprises heterogeneous procedural techniques. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes of CVEA in refractory VAs and outline practical techniques of CVEA. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation at our center between December 2017 and December 2025 were screened; CVEA was performed after unsuccessful endocardial RFA. We performed CVEA using either tip injection, conventional double-balloon, or modified double-balloon techniques based on venous anatomy. RESULTS: Among 204 consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation, 55 had VAs refractory to endocardial RFA. Of these, 42 with a coronary venous electrogram preceding VA onset by >20 ms underwent CVEA, including 33 with premature ventricular contraction (PVC) and 9 with ventricular tachycardia (VT). Acute success was achieved in 32/33 patients with PVC and all patients with VT. During a median follow-up of 1,024 days, long-term success was achieved in 22 patients with PVC and 5 with VT. No association was observed between intraprocedural findings and long-term recurrence. CVEA-related procedural complications occurred in 13 patients, with no fatal events reported. Exploratory analyses suggested favorable outcomes for the modified double-balloon technique in anatomically selected cases and an association between higher ethanol volume and ethanol-related complications. CONCLUSION: In patients with VAs refractory to endocardial RFA, CVEA was associated with favorable acute and long-term outcomes, with no fatal complications. Technique selection should be tailored to the venous anatomy, with judicious ethanol volume adjustment.

title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification. METHODS: Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite. RESULTS: Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

title: Physical activity, atrial fibrillation and the dose-response relationship: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Regular physical activity (PA) may reduce atrial fibrillation (AF) risk in the general population, however, contemporary data suggests individuals engaging in the highest levels of PA may exhibit a paradoxical rise in AF risk. The point at which the dose-response curve reverses remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between PA and AF across the full continuum of PA exposure. METHODS: Four databases were searched (from January 1990 to June 2025). Eligible studies included those that reported PA exposure compared against a sedentary control group and assessed AF incidence or prevalence. PA exposures were standardised to metabolic equivalent of task hours per week (MET-hr/wk). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using a weighted random-effects model. A weighted restricted cubic spline model of logarithmic odds was used to produce a dose-response curve. RESULTS: 37 studies were included (n = 1,298,291 individuals). In the general population, PA was associated with a reduction in odds of AF by 22% (22 studies; OR 0.78; 95% CI 0.68, 0.89). Athlete status was associated with an increase in the odds of AF (15 studies; OR 2.74; 95% CI 1.72, 4.39). Dose-response analysis (26 studies; n = 1,022,790 individuals) showed 26 MET-hr/wk of PA was associated with the greatest reduction in odds of AF, with doses beyond 78 MET-hr/wk associated with increased odds of AF; the equivalent of 6-7 hours per week of endurance training. CONCLUSION: PA and AF demonstrate a U-shaped relationship whereby beyond a quantitative dose threshold of 78 MET-hr/wk, the protective effect of exercise may reverse.

title: Enhanced Early Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock Using Machine Learning: A Hierarchical Clustering Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity, limiting the performance of conventional risk stratification tools like the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system. Machine learning (ML) has identified reproducible CS phenotypes that improve risk prediction, but their temporal consistency across the progression of shock remains incompletely described. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the temporal evolution of ML-derived CS phenotypes across the first 3 intensive care unit (ICU) days and determine whether phenotype trajectories enhance mortality stratification beyond SCAI staging. METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective registry of 2,906 adults with CS admitted to ICUs between 2016 and 2022, hierarchical agglomerative clustering was applied independently to clinical variables on ICU days 1, 2, and 3. RESULTS: On day 1, 3 phenotypes emerged: Cardiac (younger, acute myocardial infarction-predominant, preserved renal function; 15% mortality), Cardio-Renal (older, non-acute myocardial infarction-predominant, isolated renal extracardiac impairment, predominantly SCAI A and B on admission; 27% mortality), and Cardio-Metabolic (severe renal and tissue malperfusion, predominantly SCAI D and E on admission; 55% mortality). Similar phenotypes persisted on day 2 and day 3. These ML-derived phenotypes enhanced mortality stratification within each SCAI stage across days 1 to 3. CONCLUSIONS: Hierarchical clustering reproduced previously identified CS phenotypes that were consistent across the first 3 days of ICU stay, providing an enhanced framework for early risk stratification. Prospective validation is required for clinical implementation.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: Association of Air Pollution Exposure and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Consistent evidence indicates that air pollution negatively impacts cardiovascular health. However, the relationship between air pollution and atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear, and exposure measurement error has been a significant concern for prior studies. OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the association of chronic air pollution exposure and risk of AF. METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, a community-based cohort study conducted in 6 U.S. metropolitan areas. Concentrations of 4 pollutants (PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and O3) were assessed from 2000-2018 using hierarchical spatiotemporal models that incorporated cohort-specific monitoring to estimate ambient exposure at participants' residences. In Cox regression models, pollution estimates were represented as time-varying exposures, with 2-year rolling averages updated every 30 days. In our primary model, we adjusted for demographics and health behaviors. RESULTS: Our study included 6618 participants (mean age 62; 53% female). Over 16.5 years median follow-up, we identified 1055 AF events. In our primary model, an interquartile range increment of NO2 (13.5 ppb) was associated with 29% higher risk of AF (hazard ratio 95% CI: 1.00, 1.67). Associations with PM2.5, NOx, and O3 were weaker but also directionally consistent with higher risk. CONCLUSION: We found evidence linking air pollution exposure to risk of incident AF. These results can be used to inform policy and other public health efforts aimed at alleviating the burden of AF, especially given that NO2 exposure estimates (median 17.3 ppb) fell well below the current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency annual standard of 53 ppb.

title: Underserved communities at risk of heart failure: effectiveness of community-based recruitment strategies and burden of unrecognised cardiovascular disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients from socioeconomically deprived and ethnically diverse backgrounds are under-represented in cardiovascular research. EARLY-HF is a community-based pilot study designed to predict incident HF in primary care. We aimed to assess effectiveness of recruitment strategies for engaging underserved populations and quantify the burden of unrecognised CVD. METHODS: Prospective cohort study enrolling 550 adults aged ≥50 years with two or more cardiometabolic risk factors and no prior diagnosis of HF. Participants were recruited via: (i) targeted identification using electronic health records in eight primary care centres; (ii) digital advertising and targeted social media campaign; (iii) ten community outreach events; (iv) direct referral from family or friends. The baseline study visit included ECG, blood sampling, and imaging. RESULTS: 185 (34%) participants were from the most deprived Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintile and 97 (18%) were of non-White ethnicity. Primary care and digital advertising were the most effective recruitment strategies, enrolling 444 (81%) and 68 (12%) participants respectively, while maintaining diverse representation. The social media campaign generated 15,207 advertisement clicks and 1,012 expressions of interest at a cost of £5.93 per sign-up. Community outreach events enrolled 5 (1%) participants and were resource intensive. A substantial burden of previously unrecognised CVD was identified: 125 (23%) participants had clinically actionable cardiac abnormalities, including 46 (9%) with previously unrecognised myocardial infarction, 331 (60%) had uncontrolled blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg), and 162 (30%) had elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/ml). CONCLUSIONS: Primary care-embedded and digital recruitment strategies can effectively engage underserved communities at risk of HF, at scale and at low cost. This population has a very high burden of unrecognised CVD.

title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

title: Anticoagulation strategies during peripheral ultrafiltration in diuretic-resistant congestive heart failure.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Peripheral ultrafiltration (UF) is an effective strategy for the management of diuretic-resistant congestion in patients with decompensated heart failure. However, extracorporeal circuit clotting remains one of the main technical limitations of the procedure, and the optimal anticoagulation strategy during UF has not been clearly established. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different anticoagulation strategies during UF. Methods This prospective, nonrandomized, single-center study included 87 consecutive patients who underwent UF between January 2021 and November 2025. The anticoagulation strategy was tailored according to the patients' baseline anticoagulant therapy: unfractionated heparin (UFH), n = 8; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), n = 41; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), n = 12; and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), n = 26. Procedural efficacy was defined as successful completion of the UF session without premature interruption due to extracorporeal circuit dysfunction or clinical complications. Results Baseline characteristics and UF technical parameters were comparable among groups (P > .1). Procedural efficacy was highest with intravenous heparin (UFH = 100%, LMWH = 48.7%, VKAs = 66.6%, and DOACs = 65.4%; P = .048). Extracorporeal circuit clotting was more frequent with subcutaneous heparin (UFH = 0%, LMWH = 31.7%, VKAs = 25%, and DOACs = 27%; P = .018). Conclusions UFH was associated with a lower rate of extracorporeal circuit clotting and a higher rate of successful UF completion. Complications were infrequent. Given the observational design and the small sample size, these findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

title: Associations of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 Activity With Markers of Endothelial Dysfunction and Oxidative Stress in Young Healthy Adults: The African-PREDICT Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system plays a major role in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease through, among others, endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Circulating ACE2 (angiotensin-converting enzyme 2) is emerging as a biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk; however, its role in younger populations is not well-established. This study aimed to investigate sex differences in serum ACE2 activity and associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers in young, apparently healthy men and women. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we included 1134 young (aged 20-30 years) men (n=557) and women (n=577). Serum ACE2 activity was measured using a validated fluorometric assay. We analyzed markers of endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and antioxidant capacity. We performed a 2-sample t test and Mann-Whitney U test. We applied multivariable-adjusted Tobit regression analysis to account for left truncation. RESULTS: Men had higher ACE2 activity than women (P<0.001). After multiple adjustments for covariates, ACE2 activity was positively associated with von Willebrand factor (P=0.006), and a disintegrin-like metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motif type 1 member 13 (P=0.019) in men. Among women, ACE2 activity was negatively associated with asymmetric dimethylarginine (P=0.043) and superoxide dismutase (P=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Serum ACE2 activity was higher in men than women and showed sex-specific associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers. Our results suggest an association between ACE2 shedding and pathophysiological processes associated with alterations in endothelial integrity and early endothelial dysfunction, which may be influenced by sex. This highlights the role of circulating ACE2 as a potential early biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk in young adults. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03292094.

title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
abstract: AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo. METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers. RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

title: Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups.
abstract: AIMS: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. METHODS: We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. RESULTS: Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). CONCLUSION: RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups.

title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models. METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially. CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals. RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.
